files.name: CHANGELOG.md
files.body: IntroVox grows from one welcome tour into tours for Nextcloud and its apps. The major version marks that, and a few changes to the app's HTTP routes that a script outside the app could notice; the stored tours, steps and settings carry over as they are. ### Upgrade notes - **Nothing new reaches users until an admin switches it on.** App tours, the built-in tours for Files, Talk, Deck and Calendar, and the Dashboard checklist all start switched off. The one exception is **Tours** in the user menu, which everyone sees; hide it under **Settings**. - **The personal "disable the tour" switch now covers every tour.** A repair step (`IntroduceTours`) turns tours off for people who had switched the welcome tour off without finishing it; people who finished or skipped it will get app tours once an admin switches one on. - **Telemetry waits for an admin.** It is sent only after an admin has opened IntroVox's settings and been asked, once per instance. Until then an updated instance sends nothing. - **Changes for scripts that call IntroVox's routes directly:** - `POST /admin/step`, `PUT /admin/step/{id}` and `DELETE /admin/step/{id}` are gone; use `POST /admin/steps` (see Removed). - `GET /api/steps` needs a logged-in user and the CSRF request token; it was public. - The admin `GET` routes, the personal settings and `POST /api/wizard/{start,complete,skip}` need the request token too. - `POST /admin/settings` ignores `showToAll`; use `POST /admin/tours/welcome/reshow`. - **Older step exports still import**, but a step is now checked like one saved in the editor: an id of letters, digits, `_`, `.` and `-`, a title of at most 500 characters, a known position, and a file of at most 1 MB. Exports made with IntroVox pass; a hand-made file may be refused. ### Added - **Tours for apps and pages.** Besides the welcome tour, an admin can make a short tour that starts the first time someone opens an app, such as Talk or Deck, or another page of Nextcloud. Each tour has its own steps and languages, can be limited to groups, and can go to everyone or only to people who log in for the first time after it was switched on. It starts once per user, once the app has loaded, and never on top of another tour: someone new gets the welcome tour first. A new tour starts switched off. See [Tours](docs/admin/tours.md). - **Users can start every tour themselves**, from a list in their personal settings that says which ones they have seen. - **Statistics per tour, and how far people get.** The Statistics pane shows each tour on its own: how many people started, finished and skipped it, and for every step how many got at least that far, so you can see where people stop. Counted per person, only for runs that started by themselves, and only as totals; none of it is sent with the usage statistics. See [Statistics](docs/admin/tours.md#statistics). - **Move a whole tour to another Nextcloud.** **Export tour** downloads one `.zip` with the tour's settings, its steps in every language and its images and videos; **Import tour** adds it as a new tour, switched off, uploaded or from your own Files. Groups and media this Nextcloud cannot take are left out and named. A package is checked as strictly as an upload. See [Move a tour to another Nextcloud](docs/admin/tours.md#move-a-tour-to-another-nextcloud). - **Built-in tours for Files, Talk, Deck and Calendar**, switched off until you switch them on, and translated like the welcome tour. Each lets users do the app's main job once with their own work (make and share a folder, set up a team conversation, add a card with a due date, plan an event) and then shows what matters most at work, in 11 steps, written from the Nextcloud documentation and reviewed for adoption, accuracy and robust selectors. Their steps can be changed per language and reset; who gets them and when can be set like for any tour. See [Built-in tours](docs/admin/tours.md#built-in-tours). - **Share a tour with a link.** **Copy link** in a tour's menu gives a link that opens the tour's page and starts the tour there, for a welcome mail or a message to a team. It works like a start by hand: also for people who saw the tour, only for people who may get it, and not counted in the statistics. While the tour is switched off, **Copy link** says the link starts nothing yet. See [Share a tour with a link](docs/admin/tours.md#share-a-tour-with-a-link). - **"Tours" in the user menu**, just above Help, leads everyone to their tours in the personal settings. An admin can hide it under Settings. - **When a tour starts by itself:** not before a number of days after someone's first login, and only between two dates. Starting it by hand or with a link always works. - **Tours that start anywhere**, on whichever page someone opens next: with a number of days, a tip that comes once someone has found their way. - **Steps that wait for the user.** A step whose element only appears after the user did something (a conversation they create, a file's sharing they open) stands aside in the corner, leaves the page usable, and moves to the element as soon as it is there. Together with "Click on the element", a tour can now lead someone through creating a conversation and adding people, in any app. The element picker says so when the element was reached by using the page. **Continue with: Filling in the field** keeps Next off until a field has text, such as a new conversation's name. The element a step points at has a clear outline and a blinking arrow, also inside dialogs. See [Steps that wait for the user](docs/admin/managing-steps.md#steps-that-wait-for-the-user). - **"Getting started" on the Dashboard.** An admin can offer everyone a checklist of first things to do: take the welcome tour, upload a file, add a profile picture, install the app, send a message in Talk, secure the account with two-factor authentication. Each task links to where it is done and ticks itself off once the user did it. Admins can add tasks of their own, such as "Open Talk" or the folder with the handbook, ticked off once opened from the list. Off by default; the admin picks the tasks and can put the list on every Dashboard, and everyone can remove it under Customize. See [Checklist on the Dashboard](docs/admin/settings.md#checklist-on-the-dashboard). - **Translate a tour, or write its steps, with AI.** With a provider for the Nextcloud Assistant set up, **Translate with AI** translates a tour's steps into other languages, words only, and **Write steps with AI** writes new steps from a description. You check and can change every step before it is saved. See [Write or translate steps with AI](docs/admin/tours.md#write-or-translate-steps-with-ai). - **Images, GIFs and videos in steps.** A step can show one image (PNG, JPEG), animated GIF or video (MP4, WebM) above its text: uploaded, chosen from the admin's own Files, or pasted as a screenshot. A description is required unless the image is decorative; videos play with a play button or silently like a GIF, and can have captions. Anything that moves can be paused, and stays still for people with reduced motion. Only files from this Nextcloud: IntroVox keeps its own copy, checks the real file type and strips metadata such as location, and only users who get the step can load the file. See [Image or video](docs/admin/managing-steps.md#image-or-video) and the [threat model](docs/security/media.md). - **Pick the element a step points at instead of typing a CSS selector.** **Pick element** in the step editor opens Nextcloud full-screen on the settings page: click the element, and a selector that survives reloads, other languages and most updates is filled in, with a matching tooltip position. To pick something inside a menu, open the menu in Browse mode and Shift-click the item; the step then opens that menu itself before it shows (new **Open first** field). - **Tours can span apps.** A step can belong to a page, such as `/apps/spreed/` for Talk; the tour opens that app when it gets there and carries on, with Back working the same way. Pick element fills the page in. Steps in an app a user can't open are skipped, and a tour that went to other apps returns to the homepage on Done. - **Steps that continue on a click.** With **Continue with: Click on the element**, users click the highlighted element ("Click New conversation") instead of a Next button, and the step tells them so. If the element is missing, a Next button appears instead. - **Preview the tour before users get it.** **Preview tour** runs the tour for the language being edited, optionally as a member of one group; **Test this step** shows a single step, unsaved edits included. A preview is not counted in the statistics and does not mark the tour as seen for the admin. - **Step texts are written with formatting instead of HTML.** The **Text** field is an editor that shows the text as the tour will, with a toolbar for bold, italic, a heading, lists, links, code and emoji; the title has an emoji button too. Links open in a new tab, so the tour stays where it is. **Edit as HTML** shows the HTML itself. HTML that users never see, because the tour removes it, is left out of the editor with a line saying what; it only goes from the stored text once the text is changed. Texts are still stored as HTML: exports, imports and the translated default steps are unaffected. - **A short tour of the admin page for every admin**, the first time they open IntroVox's settings: the parts of the page, languages, how to make a step in four moves, the preview, and a link to the manual. It uses the same tour users get. **Show the admin tour again** under **Support** runs it again. - **Steps can be reordered without a mouse.** Every step has **Move up** and **Move down** buttons beside the drag handle. Reordering was drag-only, so it could not be done from the keyboard or with a screen reader at all — the two buttons save the new order the same way a drag does. - **Translations in 105 languages**, from Transifex as they stood on release day. Danish is complete; Spanish, Dutch and French are largely translated, partly by machine and not yet reviewed by their language teams. Languages with only a few translated strings are included too: what is not translated shows in English. ### Changed - **The Steps pane is now Tours**: a list of the tours, each with a switch, **Edit steps**, a preview, **Show again to everyone** and, for app tours, **Delete**. The step editor opens from there. The main switch is called **Tours for everyone**. - **"Permanently disable the introduction tour" in the personal settings is now "Start tours by themselves"**, and covers every tour. Users who had switched the tour off there keep tours off after the update; users who finished or skipped it get app tours. - **Show wizard to all users is now Show again to everyone**, in the welcome tour's menu under **Tours**, like for every other tour. It no longer overrides people who switched tours off; everyone else who saw the welcome tour gets it again, as before. - **The Statistics pane counts people, not clicks**, for skipping too: "Times skipped" is now "Users skipped". - **Pages load less.** The script every page loads is 18 KB instead of 252 KB, and asks the server nothing: it decides from what the page already carries whether a tour starts, and only then loads the tour itself. - **A same-origin frame of another app starts no tour inside it.** - **Wording follows Nextcloud's own terms**: people and accounts instead of "users" where it means everyone, and no contractions such as "don't" in the new strings. - **The English source strings use American spelling**, as Nextcloud itself does: "customise" became "customize". Until translators catch up, that one string shows in English in the languages that had it translated. - **Every change to the steps is saved straight away**: saving a step, deleting, reordering and switching a step on or off. The **Save changes** button only appears to retry a save that failed. The personal "disable the tour" switch saves straight away too. - **Steps are edited in a dialog, a page at a time**: content, element, behavior and who sees it. New steps walk through the pages; existing ones can be saved from any page. Element, page and menu are summarised next to **Pick element**, with the fields folded away under **Edit by hand**. The step list itself no longer expands an editor. - **The admin and personal settings pages use Nextcloud's own components and icons** instead of emoji buttons and plain form fields. Buttons show their intended colours again; with @nextcloud/vue 9 every one of them had rendered as a plain grey button. - **The tabs across the top of the admin page are Nextcloud's own pane switcher**, the control core uses for a settings page with several parts. They were hand-built buttons: a screen reader heard four loose buttons with nothing saying they belonged together or which one was open. On a phone the row no longer runs off the side of the screen — the fourth tab used to be unreachable, because the page does not scroll sideways. - **Text in the tour and on both settings pages follows the sizes the theme sets.** Sizes were fixed in the code, four of them smaller than Nextcloud's smallest — a size no display setting could enlarge. They now scale with the rest of the interface. - **Lists in a step show bullets.** Nextcloud's stylesheet takes them off every list, so a list in the tour looked like a column of indented lines. This shows in the default steps too. - **Telemetry is only sent once an admin has been asked.** The admin tour ends with the question, with a list of what is sent; it is asked once per instance. After that telemetry is on unless an admin chose not to share, as before. Instances where nobody opened IntroVox's settings since the update send nothing. The list of what is sent now also names the tour counts, the country, Docker and the license key. ### Removed - **Three unused admin endpoints**: `POST /admin/step`, `PUT /admin/step/{id}` and `DELETE /admin/step/{id}`. The app has always saved the step list as a whole through `POST /admin/steps`; nothing called these. Anything outside the app that did call them must move to `POST /admin/steps`. ### Fixed - **A fallback selector won over the main one**: with an element such as `.cards, #navigation a`, a step pointed at whichever came first in the page, here the navigation. The selectors are now tried in the order they were written. - **People with a regional language, such as `pt_BR`, `zh_CN` or `es_419`, got the welcome tour in English**: only the first two letters of a language were used, so a translation or an administrator's own steps for the full language were never shown. Now the full language comes first, then its base language. - **A welcome tour with every step switched off, or only with steps for other groups, showed the built-in steps** to the people it was meant to show nothing. It shows nothing now. - **Edited and new steps were gone after a reload.** Save in the step editor only updated the list in the browser; nothing reached the server until a separate Save changes button at the top of the list was clicked, and leaving the page did not warn. - **Cancel deleted saved steps.** Cancelling the editor removed any step that had once been created with Add step, even one saved long before. - **The tour started about ten seconds late on Nextcloud 34 and 35**, also after "Restart tour now". It waited for the inline app bar of older versions, which no longer exists, until a timeout. - **A new element for the Files, Search or Settings default step was ignored**; the tour kept pointing at the built-in one. - **Steps pointing into the apps menu lost it as soon as the mouse moved** to the tour's tooltip: Nextcloud 35 closes that menu 180 ms after the pointer leaves it. The tour now keeps the menu open for as long as the step shows. This affected the built-in Files step too. - **On instances installed in a subdirectory or without pretty URLs, users could get the built-in tour instead of the admin's.** The tour fetched its steps from a hard-coded address that does not exist there, and fell back to the bundled defaults. - **Bold words in a step looked like links.** They were shown in the same blue as a real link, so in the built-in "Important features" step "apps menu", "avatar" and "search bar" invited a click that did nothing. Bold is now bold: the colour is the text colour, and blue again means a link. This applies to every step, including ones written by an admin or a translator. - **The highlight around the element a step points at follows the server's colour.** It was always Nextcloud blue, so on an instance with its own brand colour the outline took the brand colour and the glow around it stayed blue. - **The language picker in the step editor had no name a screen reader could read.** It is labelled "Language" now, as is the one in the **Add language override** dialog. - **The close button in the tour showed its own tooltip on hover**, which repeated the label a screen reader already reads and could not be dismissed with Escape. The button keeps its name; the extra tooltip is gone. - **The tour dialog and the settings pages line up with the rest of Nextcloud again.** The tour's header was a grey band with a blue title; the tabs, the step list and the Support page each started at a different distance from the left edge of the page. - **A failed load of the step list looked like an empty tour.** Adding a step to it would have replaced the whole tour for that language. The admin page now shows an error with a Try again button, and adding steps or previewing waits until the list has loaded. - **The text field of a step showed "HTML content placeholder" as its placeholder**, a translation key that never got a text. - **Less motion where people asked for it.** With reduced motion switched on, the tour and the step list jump to a step instead of scrolling smoothly. The arrow and the outline around a step's element blink a few times and then stay still, for everyone, instead of blinking for as long as the step shows. - **The full-screen Nextcloud page of Pick element and Preview tour kept the admin page reachable**: Tab and a screen reader could leave the overlay for the page underneath. That page is now out of reach until the overlay closes. - **The pause button of a GIF or video kept a blue tint after a click**, and showed a tooltip that repeated its label. - **The app's icon was a solid disc in the app list**, and white on white where Nextcloud shows it on a light background. It is drawn again from filled shapes, for 20 pixels. ### Security - **Media in steps is checked by its content.** The type of an image or video is taken from its bytes, never from its name; SVG, HTML and every type other than PNG, JPEG, GIF, MP4, WebM and WebVTT captions are refused. Location and other metadata are stripped before the file is stored, and size, pixels, frames and total storage are limited. See the [threat model](docs/security/media.md). - **Media is only served to people who get the step**, as a download that can do nothing on its own: `nosniff`, `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; sandbox` and `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-origin`. - **Step text is sanitized in the browser as well**, with DOMPurify and a strict allowlist, wherever it is shown as HTML: in the tour, in the step list and in the AI review. - **Tour packages trust nothing.** File names, sizes and the number of files are checked before anything is unpacked, and every tour, step and file goes through the same checks as one made in the editor. - **Rate limits** on the tracking routes and on the AI routes. - **Every route needs the CSRF request token**, also the ones that only read, except two that cannot send one and only read or redirect: `GET /media/{file}`, which an `` or `

This shows in the default steps too. - **Telemetry is only sent once an admin has been asked.** The admin tour ends with the question, with a list of what is sent; it is asked once per instance. After that telemetry is on unless an admin chose not to share, as before. Instances where nobody opened IntroVox's settings since the update send nothing. The list of what is sent now also names the tour counts, the country, Docker and the license key. ### Removed - **Three unused admin endpoints**: `POST /admin/step`, `PUT /admin/step/{id}` and `DELETE /admin/step/{id}`. The app has always saved the step list as a whole through `POST /admin/steps`; nothing called these. Anything outside the app that did call them must move to `POST /admin/steps`. ### Fixed - **A fallback selector won over the main one**: with an element such as `.cards, #navigation a`, a step pointed at whichever came first in the page, here the navigation. The selectors are now tried in the order they were written. - **People with a regional language, such as `pt_BR`, `zh_CN` or `es_419`, got the welcome tour in English**: only the first two letters of a language were used, so a translation or an administrator's own steps for the full language were never shown. Now the full language comes first, then its base language. - **A welcome tour with every step switched off, or only with steps for other groups, showed the built-in steps** to the people it was meant to show nothing. It shows nothing now. - **Edited and new steps were gone after a reload.** Save in the step editor only updated the list in the browser; nothing reached the server until a separate Save changes button at the top of the list was clicked, and leaving the page did not warn. - **Cancel deleted saved steps.** Cancelling the editor removed any step that had once been created with Add step, even one saved long before. - **The tour started about ten seconds late on Nextcloud 34 and 35**, also after "Restart tour now". It waited for the inline app bar of older versions, which no longer exists, until a timeout. - **A new element for the Files, Search or Settings default step was ignored**; the tour kept pointing at the built-in one. - **Steps pointing into the apps menu lost it as soon as the mouse moved** to the tour's tooltip: Nextcloud 35 closes that menu 180 ms after the pointer leaves it. The tour now keeps the menu open for as long as the step shows. This affected the built-in Files step too. - **On instances installed in a subdirectory or without pretty URLs, users could get the built-in tour instead of the admin's.** The tour fetched its steps from a hard-coded address that does not exist there, and fell back to the bundled defaults. - **Bold words in a step looked like links.** They were shown in the same blue as a real link, so in the built-in "Important features" step "apps menu", "avatar" and "search bar" invited a click that did nothing. Bold is now bold: the colour is the text colour, and blue again means a link. This applies to every step, including ones written by an admin or a translator. - **The highlight around the element a step points at follows the server's colour.** It was always Nextcloud blue, so on an instance with its own brand colour the outline took the brand colour and the glow around it stayed blue. - **The language picker in the step editor had no name a screen reader could read.** It is labelled "Language" now, as is the one in the **Add language override** dialog. - **The close button in the tour showed its own tooltip on hover**, which repeated the label a screen reader already reads and could not be dismissed with Escape. The button keeps its name; the extra tooltip is gone. - **The tour dialog and the settings pages line up with the rest of Nextcloud again.** The tour's header was a grey band with a blue title; the tabs, the step list and the Support page each started at a different distance from the left edge of the page. - **A failed load of the step list looked like an empty tour.** Adding a step to it would have replaced the whole tour for that language. The admin page now shows an error with a Try again button, and adding steps or previewing waits until the list has loaded. - **The text field of a step showed "HTML content placeholder" as its placeholder**, a translation key that never got a text. - **Less motion where people asked for it.** With reduced motion switched on, the tour and the step list jump to a step instead of scrolling smoothly. The arrow and the outline around a step's element blink a few times and then stay still, for everyone, instead of blinking for as long as the step shows. - **The full-screen Nextcloud page of Pick element and Preview tour kept the admin page reachable**: Tab and a screen reader could leave the overlay for the page underneath. That page is now out of reach until the overlay closes. - **The pause button of a GIF or video kept a blue tint after a click**, and showed a tooltip that repeated its label. - **The app's icon was a solid disc in the app list**, and white on white where Nextcloud shows it on a light background. It is drawn again from filled shapes, for 20 pixels. ### Security - **Media in steps is checked by its content.** The type of an image or video is taken from its bytes, never from its name; SVG, HTML and every type other than PNG, JPEG, GIF, MP4, WebM and WebVTT captions are refused. Location and other metadata are stripped before the file is stored, and size, pixels, frames and total storage are limited. See the [threat model](docs/security/media.md). - **Media is only served to people who get the step**, as a download that can do nothing on its own: `nosniff`, `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; sandbox` and `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-origin`. - **Step text is sanitized in the browser as well**, with DOMPurify and a strict allowlist, wherever it is shown as HTML: in the tour, in the step list and in the AI review. - **Tour packages trust nothing.** File names, sizes and the number of files are checked before anything is unpacked, and every tour, step and file goes through the same checks as one made in the editor. - **Rate limits** on the tracking routes and on the AI routes. - **Every route needs the CSRF request token**, also the ones that only read, except two that cannot send one and only read or redirect: `GET /media/{file}`, which an `` or `
